INSURANCE FRAUD

By: Ntokozo Miya | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Burned bodies, millions in payouts, and law enforcers on the chase – we investigate what it is about the life insurance industry that makes it fertile ground for fraudsters and even worse, murderers

Unique Selling Point:
Over and above getting to understand life insurance sector fraud, we meet the families involved in the latest insurance fraud scheme to hit the headlines, the Soshanguve matter.

Summary:
After a man and his wife successfully staged the man's death in January 2022, the wife submitted an insurance claim. The insurer paid out an amount believed to be close to R2 million. The wife then joined her husband in Mpumalanga where he was hiding, playing dead. The pair moved around from area to area, avoiding questions and detection. When funds were low only a year later, the couple then decided that the wife should return to Soshanguve and try and get a job until they figure out their next step.

To keep himself entertained while the wife is in Soshanguve, the husband finds himself a girlfriend. But he misses his wife so he takes his girlfriend's car, picks up his wife and they find a spot to hideout near Hammanskraal. He avoids his girlfriend's calls and her queries about her car.

Frustrated and angry, the girlfriend reports the car stolen. Whie taking a drive about 2 weeks ago, the man encounters a routine traffic stop but is so nervous that police take him to the station for interrogation. The man confesses that he is nervous because he can't have his prints taken... the reason: officially, he “died and was buried” in January 2022. He details the plot below in his confession to police.

The victim, whose remains were passed off as those of Sibusiso Mahlangu, is Sibusiso Sithebe. Sithebe is Lerato's ex-boyfriend and the father of her 10-year-old daughter. Sithebe was killed in the couple's home. They attempted to set him alight but the fire did not do enough damage to make Sithebe unrecognisable. The officer who was investigating the “death” of the man identified by Lerato and Mahlangu's mother as Sibusiso Mahlangu, kept the photos of the victim in his file. After Mahlangu confessed that man who was buried in his place was actually Sithebe, the photos were shown to Lerato's aunt, Joyce and Sithebe's family. They were able to identify the man in the photo as Sibusiso Sithebe who the Sithebes had been looking for since December 2021.

Further information:
We also speak to the Forensics head of ASISA, an organisation that represents insurance companies. Megan Govender breaks down the weeknesses in insurance processes, the types of insurance frauds as well as how the industry is fighting back to protect honest customers and prevent huge financial losses.

We also include the court proceedings from the court appearance on Thursday 18 May 2023.

Additionally, in the place of a couple of links, the presenter talks about other horrific incidents of deaths involving insurance fraud.

Press Release:


Dead Man Driving
In April this year, police in Gauteng tracked a stolen vehicle in Hammanskraal . In a panic, the man behind the wheel, told officers a bizarre story that had them investigating a new case - an elaborate scheme involving murder and an insurance pay-out close to R2 million. It turned out that a year earlier, the driver – Sibusiso Mahlangu – had orchestrated his own death, apparently dying in a tragic house fire. Instead, the badly burnt body found in the rubble, was another man – Sibusiso Sithebe – Mahlanugu’s wife’s former lover. Mahlangu’s wife and co-conspirator, Lerato, claimed the multi-million rand insurance pay-out and for a while at least, the couple lived undetected. But in April, the wheels came off their devious plan. Now the couple is facing multiple charges including murder.
Producer: Ntokozo Sindane | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

INSURANCE FRAUD – POST-SECOND VIEWING

AUDIO
BREATHER
VO – It’s a story that's shaken a community in Soshanguve, just north of Pretoria...

PAUSE

VO - A tale of two Sibusisos... the first - Sibusiso Sithebe, a man who went missing early last year...

PAUSE

VO - … the second - Sibusiso Mahlangu, believed to have died… also in early 2022.

PAUSE

VO - And at its core... Mahlangu's widow, Lerato... who would become a central figure in this treacherous saga…
BREATHER – add 2 seconds to breather, let it linger
VO – Lerato is raised by her aunt, Joyce Mokgolobotho...

PAUSE

VO - ...affectionately known as Mama Joyce, she's proud of how Lerato was brought up.
JOYCE MOKGOLOBOTHO – LERATO'S AUNT

She was a good child, like any other child who was raised well and taught respect.
VO - In her twenties, Lerato is employed by an insurance company.
JOYCE MOKGOLOBOTHO – LERATO'S AUNT

She was funny, had friends and loved people.
VO - ...and falls in love with a hardworking taxi driver.

[PAUSE]

Embraced by her family, he's the first Sibusiso in this drama... Sibusiso Sithebe.
BREATHER
VO – Initially, the relationship thrives and in 2014, Lerato and Sibusiso have a daughter.
PAUSE
VO - Linah is Sibusiso's sister.
LINAH SITHEBE – VICTIM'S SISTER

She looks like her father. She’s a spitting image of her father
VO – But Lerato and Sibusiso Sithebe grow apart, and they separate soon after their daughter is born.

[PAUSE]

And it’s here that the story has its first significant twist…
BREATHER
VO - Enter, the second Sibusiso… surname, Mahlangu.

[PAUSE]

After the break-up, Lerato falls in love with this Sibusiso...

But, unlike Sithebe, her new love doesn’t hit it off with Lerato’s family.
JOYCE MOKGOLOBOTHO – LERATO'S AUNT

Sibusiso - what I didn't like about him is that he was disrespectful.
VO - Nonetheless, Lerato and Sibusiso Mahlangu get married in 2018.
JOYCE MOKGOLOBOTHO – LERATO'S AUNT

Lerato changed after marrying Sibusiso. When we had family gatherings, Lerato didn’t attend.
BREATHER – add 2 more seconds for breather
VO – Then, the next twist: In January 2022, Mama Joyce gets a frantic call... from Lerato... saying the house she shares with Mahlangu is on fire.
BREATHER
JOYCE MOKGOLOBOTHO – LERATO'S AUNT

One boy went inside after they broke in. He said that there was someone on the bed. They thought it was Sibusiso.

CLAIRE - Did you see the body come out of the house?

The police didn’t allow anyone to get close
BREATHER – add 2 more seconds for breather
VO – Horrified by Sibusiso Mahlangu's death in the fire, local activist, Given Moraba, and others in the community step in to help.
GIVEN MORABA – COMMUNITY LEADER

We provided support in the form of braai packs and such things, for Mahlangu to be buried in peace
BREATHER – add 2 more seconds for breather
VO – Lerato will soon collect close to R2 million from a life insurance policy.
BREATHER
VO – As this is unfolding, another Soshanguve family is grappling with tragedy. Sibusiso Sithebe, the father of Lerato’s child, has disappeared.
BREATHER – add 2 more seconds for breather
VO – His famiy makes frantic calls - including to Lerato.
LINAH SITHEBE – VICTIM'S SISTER

Lerato told me that I was stressing her.

CLAIRE – Didn’t you know there was a death in her family?

I didn’t know. I found out that day that her husband had died.
VO - Weeks turn into months and then into a year without word from Sibusiso Sithebe.
BREATHER – upsound police radio activity – keep raising and lowering this audio over suspensful music from here up until VO further down that ends with “policy after his supposed death.”
VO – Then, the story’s next and most significant twist... in April this year, Pretoria police pull over a car they suspect has been stolen.
BREATHER – upsound police radio activity
VO – When they question him, the panicked driver makes a wild confession: he’s a co-conspirator in his own faked death; succumbing to a fire at his home in Soshanguve the year before.

PAUSE

VO – The driver – is in fact - Sibusiso Mahlangu... whose wife, Lerato, cashed in close to two million rand from an insurance policy after his supposed death.

PAUSE – big reveal...

VO – Then, the final, tragic twist: the real deceased – and the body retrieved from the smoldering house around a year earlier – is Sibusiso Sithebe, Lerato's former lover and the father of her child.

PAUSE – big reveal...
VO – Later, Mama Joyce and Linah are called to the police station and shown photos of the person killed in the fire.
JOYCE MOKGOLOBOTHO – LERATO'S AUNT

The officer opened a file. It had about 3 photos of the person who died. I said, “This is Sibusiso Sithebe.

CLAIRE – Immediately?

Yes.
LINAH SITHEBE – VICTIM'S SISTER

It was clear that it's our Sibusiso. You could see that it was him.
BREATHER
VO - Soon afterwards, Lerato and her husband are arrested on suspicion of murdering Sibusiso Sithebe as well as defeating the ends of justice. Mama Joyce is bewildered.
BREATHER – match music/sound as on previous section but for defeat, disbelief, shock, etc
LINK – Mama Joyce's shock is understandable because in January last year, she was among mourners gathered at this very cemetery to lay her niece's husband to rest... She had no idea that the funeral was just one link in a sinister chain of events related to an alleged murder and insurance fraud.
VO – And so began the unraveling of the bizarre case of the two Sibusisos...

[PAUSE]

...one, a devoted father, the other, a suspect in his murder.
BREATHER
VO – The Association for Savings and Investment represents major insurance and investment companies. Jean van Niekerk is the chair of its Forensics Standing Committee and says fraud and dishonesty are a massive drain on the sector.
JEAN VAN NIEKERK – ASISA

The latest stats that we had available indicated that around about 700 million of transactions were for fraudulent purposes.
VO – ...the biggest chunk of which relates to death benefits... up from around three hundred and forty-five million in 2020 to more than five hundred and eighty-eight million in 2021.
BREATHER
VO – And the biggest of these fraud cases often make for sensational headlines...
Strap - CARTE BLANCHE – SEPTEMBER 2021
VO - ...few more shocking than the case of convicted serial killer, Rosemary Nomia Ndlovu...
ROSEMARY – When a house burns, everyone in it burns.
VO - Police woman, Ndlovu, received six life sentences for arranging the murder of five relatives and her lover.  She was arrested while plotting the death of her 7th victim who she wanted killed in a house fire. Known as the Insurance Killer, she enriched herself by cashing in her victim’s life policies.
BREATHER - Transition creatively out of Carte Blanche September 2021 insert on Rosemary
JEAN VAN NIEKERK – ASISA

In South Africa, we're definitely seeing an increase in violent crimes and that obviously links into murders, into death claims.

CLAIRE - What then happens when fraud has been detected? Do we try to recoup funds, or no?

Absolutely. But I think even arguably above that, the more critical component is prosecuting these fraudsters
BREATHER - start sequence of community members arriving by bus, singing outside court with their signs
VO – At the Soshanguve Magistrates court in May, the Mahlangus abandoned their quest for bail.
UPSOUND – someone says something to Sibusiso Mahlangu in court and he nods
VO - The family of Sibusiso Mahlangu declined our request for an interview but his mother told us they know nothing about his crimes.
GIVEN MORABA – COMMUNITY LEADER

The mother also received money. She’s building a house with that money but she didn’t know that the money she got wasn’t from the death of her son. That is the problem.
VO - Police have since exhumed the body said to be Sithebe’s and await DNA results in their ongoing investigation.
JOYCE MOKGOLOBOTHO – LERATO'S AUNT

I don’t even support Lerato. They know exactly what they did to this man. They killed him. Killing is in their blood. They killed him for money.
BREATHER
LINK – The Sithebe's spent over a year looking for Sibusiso... all the time he was buried here... Furious and grief-stricken, their only wish now is to lay him to rest, in line with the family's burial rites, hoping that his spirit will finally find peace
BREATHER
VO – While Sibusiso was missing, Linah attended a friend's burial here... she probably walked past her brother's grave and didn't even know it.
LINAH SITHEBE – VICTIM'S SISTER

I still had that hope that he’s alive somewhere, being mischievous. I dreamt of him sitting with my mother in a beautiful place.

VO: A multimillion rand life insurance policy, a brutal murder and the shocking story of two men called Sibusiso.

Mama Joyce: They know exactly what they did to this man. They killed him. Killing is in their blood. They want money.

Promo 2

Linah: She told me that I was stressing her. Her husband had died.

VO: Murder, a multimillion rand life insurance policy and a shocking confession that revealed a startling story of betrayal.

Mama Joyce: They killed him. Killing is in their blood. They want money.

Promo 3

VO: One woman searches for her missing brother.

Linah: I still had that hope that he’s alive somewhere out there.

VO: Another … horrified by the crimes allegedly committed by the child she raised.

Mama Joyce: Lerato changed after marrying Sibusiso.

VO: Their worlds collide in a shocking story of betrayal.

Promo 4

An angry community, broken families, and an industry's fight against widespread fraud – we investigate a senseless murder for profit scheme, orchestrated by a Soshanguve couple that has left everyone involved in search of answers and justice.

But in April, the wheels came off their devious plan. Now the couple is facing multiple charges including murder. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Burned bodies, millions in payouts, and law enforcers on the chase – we investigate what it is about the life insurance industry that makes it fertile ground for fraudsters and even worse, murderers
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Over and above getting to understand life insurance sector fraud, we meet the families involved in the latest insurance fraud scheme to hit the headlines, the Soshanguve matter.
metadata.Summary: After a man and his wife successfully staged the man's death in January 2022, the wife submitted an insurance claim. The insurer paid out an amount believed to be close to R2 million. The wife then joined her husband in Mpumalanga where he was hiding, playing dead. The pair moved around from area to area, avoiding questions and detection. When funds were low only a year later, the couple then decided that the wife should return to Soshanguve and try and get a job until they figure out their next step. To keep himself entertained while the wife is in Soshanguve, the husband finds himself a girlfriend. But he misses his wife so he takes his girlfriend's car, picks up his wife and they find a spot to hideout near Hammanskraal. He avoids his girlfriend's calls and her queries about her car. Frustrated and angry, the girlfriend reports the car stolen. Whie taking a drive about 2 weeks ago, the man encounters a routine traffic stop but is so nervous that police take him to the station for interrogation. The man confesses that he is nervous because he can't have his prints taken... the reason: officially, he “died and was buried” in January 2022. He details the plot below in his confession to police. The victim, whose remains were passed off as those of Sibusiso Mahlangu, is Sibusiso Sithebe. Sithebe is Lerato's ex-boyfriend and the father of her 10-year-old daughter. Sithebe was killed in the couple's home. They attempted to set him alight but the fire did not do enough damage to make Sithebe unrecognisable. The officer who was investigating the “death” of the man identified by Lerato and Mahlangu's mother as Sibusiso Mahlangu, kept the photos of the victim in his file. After Mahlangu confessed that man who was buried in his place was actually Sithebe, the photos were shown to Lerato's aunt, Joyce and Sithebe's family. They were able to identify the man in the photo as Sibusiso Sithebe who the Sithebes had been looking for since December 2021.
metadata.Further information: We also speak to the Forensics head of ASISA, an organisation that represents insurance companies. Megan Govender breaks down the weeknesses in insurance processes, the types of insurance frauds as well as how the industry is fighting back to protect honest customers and prevent huge financial losses. We also include the court proceedings from the court appearance on Thursday 18 May 2023. Additionally, in the place of a couple of links, the presenter talks about other horrific incidents of deaths involving insurance fraud.
